compiler: rustc 1.95.0 (LLVM 22.1.2); release thin LTO; codegen-units=1; -C target-cpu=native (apple-m4); cargo --locked

recorded_hardware.power: battery power, 64% at start, discharging; no thermal or performance warning recorded
recorded_hardware.mac_worker_affinity: No claim of fixed core affinity or fully controlled background UI load

timing_includes: fresh thread pool, segmented sieve, validation, setup, seeds, traversal, decode, sorted collection and pool teardown
timing_excludes: compilation, fixture warmups, canonical hash, tuple comparison, printing and evidence I/O

sources.capsule_checksums: verified against RELEASE-SHA256SUMS and each capsule's own SHA256SUMS before building

commands: cycles_comparison range 200000000 200100000 generic original-m4-max.json 8   (in 8eaaab0, run after the comparison, not concurrently)
order: range-compare's rotating three-method order, three passes each; then one original generic pass
caveats: Rust 1.95.0 / LLVM 22.1.2 was used; the historical M1 and EPYC runs recorded Rust 1.98.1.
The generic_one_pass_seconds header and generic_one_pass_speedup fields in m4-max-200m.jsonl reuse the M1 oracle time, so they compare different hardware; use the same-M4 speedup above.
In m4-max-200m.jsonl only the absolute oracle_path was rewritten to the repository-relative path; all other bytes of each row are as emitted.
Original generic has one sample, as on the M1 Max; the machine ran on battery power and background UI load was not controlled.
